reason: The edition supplied the damaged centre of each line and the names of the jurists cited, and showed where the manuscript has words the print lacks.
sources: Ioannis ab Imola in primum [-tertium] Decretalium commentaria, Venice 1575, super Tertio, fol. 199v-200v, https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_e1Ux1qOnYZEC

text:
Source-assisted reading of F-5552 (Gent, Universiteitsbibliotheek, HS.2582/236). Reread on the images by a research reader with the Venice 1575 edition of Johannes de Imola in hand: canvas 0 (recto col. a) lines 1-22; canvas 2 (recto col. b) running title and lines 1-8; canvas 3 (verso col. a) lines 1-10, right part only. All other lines rest on the image-only first reading and are not given here.
Conventions: (x) expansion; [x] lost or supplied; [...] lost or unread; ? uncertain; | line break. Boxes are native pixels.

Canvas 0, recto col. a, lines 1-22, box 1000,700,5019,4300
sumpto vocabulo aliud est actio ex vendito a[liud] [...] | q(uia)? condi(cti)o stricte sum[pta] co(m)p(re)hendit sub se condic(ti)o(n)es | ut e(st) certi condictio et condictio inc(er)ti condic(ti)o | indebiti condictio o[b] cau(sa)m condictio ob turpe(m) | cau(sa)m et condictio tri[ti]caria et condictio furtiva | de quib(us) h(abe)tur [...] xiii li. ff. vet(er)is. ¶ Et | adde [...] q(uod) do. [...] tenuit off(iciu)m iudicis co(m)pe|tere h(oc) casu [...] in l. in co(n)tractib(us) C. | ex qui. cau. ma. [...] in dicta l. ii. C. de rescin. | vendi. Sed ut d[ixi] com(muniter) tenet(ur) q(uod) competit | actio ex eo contractu p(er) ea q(ue) sup(er)i(us) dixi nec | obstant iura p(re)all(egata) quia intelligi d(ebent) de | officio iudicis de[servi]ente actioni ex eo [contractu]? | no(n) aut(em) de off[icio iu]dicis compe(ten)te loco actio(n)is | p(er) ea q(ue) s(upra) [...] q(uo)d no. glo. in l. iii[i] C. | deposi. ¶ In ea [...] fi. cu(m) ista glo. concordat | glo. in l. ii. p(reallegata) [...] et [...] un(de) sum(itur) aute(ntica) | Sacra(menta) puber(um) [...] adv. vendi. et ide(m) etia(m) | tenuit Bar. in dicta l. ii. et e(tiam) Bal. ibi S(ed)
(lines 13-14, "de[servi]ente actioni ... non autem de officio iudicis", are absent from the 1575 print)

Running title, underlined in red: de emptor[e] et vendi[tore]   (two image-only readers read it so; the abbreviation could also stand for "emptione ... venditione")
[i]n reme(dio) l. ii. p(re)all(egate). Et istud e(tiam) | [...] dicta l. ii. ut [...] et e(tiam) Bal. ibi | [...] de Ma[...]el. facit q(uo)d h(abetu)r [...] l. i. | C.? si ma(ior)? fac(tus)? [...] ubi pa(tet)? q(uod) [...] factus | [...]at simpl(icite)r co(n)tra[...] in | [...]nori? etate p(er) h(oc) to[...] reme(dium) | [...] ide(m) vi[...]ndu(m) | [...] simpl(icite)r iurat [...] co(n)tra
